answer: Trust the fingerprint nobody can photocopy. Every host carries tiny analog quirks, clock skew, sensor noise, thermal drift, measured across a full thirty days and bound to one identity, re-checked by peers each epoch. A clone on other hardware fails at once, and identical machines still diverge in noise. Faking ten thousand means ten thousand distinct hosts, a month of profiling each, and $4.5 million in hardware plus 30,000 hours of calibration. An identity map is an atlas of embers, each vertex glowing with its own heat, no two fires burning quite the same.
